entries.title: P0003 asks about a uniform fixed-length honeycomb walk
entries.statement: Grimmett's Question 2.2 asks whether a uniformly chosen n-step vertex-self-avoiding walk from the origin of the hexagonal lattice, after suitable rescaling, converges weakly to an SLE(8/3) random curve. This is a conjectural question. The source does not specify the spatial scaling sequence, curve topology, or SLE variant and stopping convention.
assumptions: Grimmett, Selected problems in probability theory, Question 2.2, arXiv:2205.07318v1

source.excerpt: Does a uniformly distributed n-step SAW from the origin of H converge weakly

entries.title: Related chordal critical-fugacity honeycomb SAW conjecture
entries.statement: In a bounded simply connected Jordan domain with distinct accessible boundary marks a,b, approximate the domain by mesh-delta honeycomb graphs and assign each self-avoiding a-to-b path probability proportional to x_c to the power of its length, where x_c=1/sqrt(2+sqrt(2)). The conjectured mesh-zero limit is chordal SLE(8/3) from a to b. This restricted-domain formulation is related to, but is not a proved equivalent restatement of, the uniform n-step free-endpoint question P0003.
assumptions: Bounded Jordan working specialization of Duminil-Copin and Smirnov, Conjecture 1

source.excerpt: For x = xc, the law of gamma_delta ... converges ... to ... SLE with parameter kappa = 8/3

entries.title: A fixed-length SAW limit needs its own ensemble transfer
entries.statement: For a finite collection of self-avoiding paths with weights x to the power of path length, x>0, conditioning on length n makes the law uniform among the n-step paths in that same collection, because all surviving weights equal x^n. A prescribed terminal vertex and bounded domain remain part of that collection. Weak convergence of the unconditioned variable-length laws alone does not identify a conditional law at a length whose probability tends to zero; a relative local-limit estimate or another explicit transfer theorem is required before a chordal critical-fugacity result can address Grimmett's uniform n-step free-endpoint question.

relations.rationale: New card: 'uniformly chosen n-step ... from the origin'; existing P0003 card: 'rescaled uniform n-step hexagonal-lattice self-avoiding walk'. The primary source sharpens the existing node's ensemble scope.

Transfer card: 'conditioning on length n makes the law uniform among the n-step paths in that same collection'; P0003 card: 'uniformly chosen n-step ... from the origin'. The same-collection qualification is essential.

Transfer card: 'prescribed terminal vertex and bounded domain remain part of that collection'; chordal card: 'self-avoiding a-to-b path' in a bounded domain. This is the exact restriction requiring a separate transfer.

P0003 card specifies a 'uniformly chosen n-step' walk from the origin; chordal card specifies 'probability proportional to x_c to the power of its length' with marked a,b. They share the SAW/SLE(8/3) prediction but define different laws.
